title: Parapsychologist explains why more ghosts are seen in winter
excerpt: A parapsychologist has explained why ghosts are seen more often in winter.
content:
A parapsychologist has explained why ghosts are seen more often in winter.

Are ghosts seen more often in winter?

Ian Fairholm, a lecturer in psychology at the University of Bath who specialises in parapsychology, has lifted the lid on why witnesses are more likely to spot a spook in the colder months insisting the increase in sightings is due to the longer nights and many people are already primed for spooky season after celebrating Halloween in October.

Fairholm told the BBC: "We've just had Halloween and it's getting darker earlier. It's when we want to tell stories and swap ideas and that fits in with us being maybe a little bit more anxious."

He also gave some suggestions about what could be causing an increase in winter hauntings, explaining some ghostly noises can be due to the central heating being fired up while some could be caused by infrasound - acoustic pressure waves with frequencies below the typical limit of human hearing which are said to heighten feelings of dread.

He told the outlet: "Ghosts relate to what it means to be human, what the next state of being is. We know what it is to be alive but we don't know what comes next .

"[Some witness in old buildings] often have weird things going on in their piping or holes ... A popular theory is about infra sound, which is sound just below human hearing.

"The idea is that - even though humans can't hear it consciously - maybe it's still affecting them in some ways."

It comes after a paranormal investigator has insisted not all ghosts are "evil".

Colin Browen - who hosts the Murder In America podcast and The Paranormal Files on YouTube - has declared it's a common misconception that all hauntings are frightening and revealed he's encountered plenty of "happy, jovial spirits" who just wanted to have a bit of a "laugh".

He told the US Mirror: "I've investigated dozens of homes and places that were filled with happy, jovial spirits - in fact, one night, we spent the entire night telling jokes to the spirits and watched as they played with our devices and seemingly laughed along with us."

Colin blames Hollywood horror movies and documentaries for the negative perception of hauntings, adding: "In horror movies and documentaries about the paranormal world, usually hauntings are portrayed as intense, frightening and disturbing; however, in real life, it's never black and white.

"Although it's possible you may run into something more on the negative side, and you may not be dealing with Casper, most of the time, the spirits we encounter and interact with seem to be lost souls, in a way - not angry, demonic beings intent on raising hell - simply energies and spiritual entities that we don't really understand."

Colin went on to insist most ghosts aren't interested in hurting humans and often they just want acknowledgement or help.

He added: "[Often they want] be acknowledged ... [or] helped with a task or given some form of respect."
